prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1002; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured reported a collision at an intersection while turning left, with the claimant's vehicle reportedly struck on the driver's side. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will route through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver involved is listed as a named insured, and the policy was active at the time of loss. No coverage questions have arisen so far.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene and records the same general sequence of events the claimant described to me on first contact.

Entry 4: Photos from the scene and the shop show damage that lines up well with a left-turn impact of this kind. A few older scratches appear on the lower panels and may predate this loss; I have noted them separately for the appraiser.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant's attorney, who confirmed the injury claim is whiplash. The account given matches what the claimant said in every earlier conversation, with no changes in the timeline or details.

Entry 6: No independent witnesses have come forward. The photos confirm several details of the scene, but nothing in the file yet speaks to what happened beyond what the parties have described.

Entry 7: Medical records show the reported injury is consistent in type and force with the collision. Treatment followed a typical course and tapered as the claimant improved.

Entry 8: Prior records show a minor strain in the same area several years ago, which resolved fully without lasting effects. I have asked the medical reviewer to account for this history in the evaluation.

Entry 9: Requested the claimant's prior treatment history through the attorney for completeness. Nothing in the file so far suggests the vehicle damage occurred before the coverage start date.

Entry 10: Appraiser's estimate aligns with the described impact. Final determination on the older scratches is pending, and I will reconcile them with the repair scope.

Entry 11: File is current and awaiting the medical reviewer's note and the appraiser's final scope. Next review is scheduled once both have been received.
